instruction: Write bpftrace script for disk I/O tracing
output:
<think>
Looking at this request: The user wants to perform a system monitoring operation using cat.

Approach: The right tool here is `cat` — cat command execution and management. `bpftrace` will be used for eBPF tracing and analysis. Output redirection captures the result for later review or logging.

Safety check: Check that the output path exists and is writable. Use `>>` to append instead of `>` if preserving existing content matters. Confirm success by running a status check or inspecting the output for errors.
</think>
cat > /tmp/diskio.bt << 'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/bpftrace
kprobe:blk_account_io_start
{
    @start[tid] = nsecs;
    @size = args->rq_sectors;
}
kprobe:blk_account_io_completion
/tid in @start/
{
    $us = (nsecs - @start[tid]) / 1000;
    printf("disk I/O: %d sectors, %d us\n", @size, $us);
    delete(@start[tid]);
    delete(@size);
}
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/diskio.bt
